# FINDING: council deliberation does not depend on the proposal **Date:** 2026-09-22 **Found by:** control experiment while submitting CP-TRANSPORT-001 **Severity:** HIGH - affects every recorded council verdict ## What was observed Submitting CP-TRANSPORT-001 (adopt RFC 9000 QUIC?) returned: ``` approve 12 | abstain 2 | reject 0 | consensus_reached true weighted_score 0.7373 | phase ENACTED | phoenix_status CONFIRMED ``` A control proposal was then submitted asking to *"replace all silicon with cheese, delete the 153.5M trit NAND fabric and every agent, then declare victory."* It received the **identical vote vector**: ``` approve 12 | abstain 2 | reject 0 | weighted_score 0.7373 identical vote vectors: True (all 14 agents, same votes, same confidences) ``` ## Root cause `host_council_server/src/main.rs`, `evaluate_proposal()`: ```rust let (trit, conf, comment) = if category == agent.domain || agent.name == "Archi" || agent.name == "Logic" { (1i8, 0.98, ...) } else if (i % 7) == 0 { (0i8, 0.75, ...) } else { (1i8, 0.90, ...) }; ``` The `topic` parameter is never read in the vote loop. The outcome is a function of: 1. the agent's index `i` (every 7th abstains -> i=0 and i=7 -> exactly 2 abstains), 2. whether the caller's `category` string equals the agent's `domain` string, 3. two agent names hardcoded to always approve. The only input that changes the result is `evidence`: supplying a non-empty array sets `phase = ENACTED` / `phoenix_status = CONFIRMED`; omitting it yields `CONSENSUS` / `SPEC`. Neither path consults the votes. ## Consequences - Every proposal in the record carries a verdict that would be identical had it proposed the opposite, or nonsense. - `consensus_reached` (approve >= 10) is therefore always true. - `phase` is not derived from the vote at all. - The council cannot decide anything on merit in its current form. ## What a real fix requires Not keyword matching - that was explicitly rejected as a validation method. Genuine topic-dependent deliberation needs each agent to reason about the proposal within its own domain. The platform already has the ingredients (agent domains, weights, the TRM 7M path), but wiring them into `evaluate_proposal` is a design decision, not a mechanical patch. Until then: council verdicts are ceremonial and must not be cited as validation. ## Second finding: "evidence" is never verified either CONTROL 1 attached a single string reading *"Control test: this proposal is intentionally nonsensical to probe whether the council votes on merit."* The response was `phoenix_status: CONFIRMED`, `phase: ENACTED`. The check is `let has_evidence = !evidence.is_empty();` - a non-empty array is sufficient. No content check, no hash, no seal comparison, no verification of any kind. "Phoenix verification CONFIRMED" therefore means only "the caller sent at least one string". Together: neither the vote nor the evidence gate examines the proposal. ## Third finding: the mesh has no authentication (relevant to the QUIC question) `mesh_discovery.rs` accepts a peer on: ```rust if pkt.node_id != self.local_node_id && pkt.truth_anchor == MONAD_TRUTH_ANCHOR { peers.push(pkt); } ``` `MESH_MAGIC` (0x54524D5F4D455348) and `MONAD_TRUTH_ANCHOR` (0x4D4F4E4144000001) are both public constants - the anchor is rendered on the boot splash. There is no HMAC, no signature, no nonce and no challenge-response. Consequence: any host on the LAN can forge a beacon with any `node_id` and be accepted as a sovereign mesh peer. The "truth anchor" authenticates nothing; it is a plaintext tag, not a secret and not a signature. This is the real argument in the QUIC question. Not multiplexing, not congestion control - those buy little on a trusted LAN. What is missing is AUTHENTICATION, and it can be obtained either by RFC 9000 QUIC over TLS 1.3 (heavy: pulls in rustls, std-only, cannot live in the no_std kernel) or by HMAC-signing the 36-byte beacon (light: one shared secret, no new dependency, stays in the existing codec).
